# SUPPLY COUNTRIES — Where To Source, Outside India

**44 countries scored on 11 weighted dimensions plus 4 knockout gates.** Generated by
[`scoring/countries.py`](scoring/countries.py). Evidence tags per [`MASTER.md`](MASTER.md) §0.

> **English scores are EF EPI 2025 [V]** — 2.2 million test takers, and the first edition to
> include speaking and writing. Band thresholds: **600+ very high · 550+ high · 500+ moderate ·
> 450+ low · <450 very low.**

---

## 1. The criteria, and why they are weighted this way

| Dimension | Weight | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| **RETAIN** | 20 | Expected tenure, driven by local labour-market slack. The largest lever in the model |
| **ENG** | 18 | Usable English at the TOP of the distribution, not the national average — see the EF EPI caveat |
| **COST** | 14 | Arbitrage size: USD cost of a mid-level finance hire |
| **DEPTH** | 12 | Pool of qualified people in OUR five roles |
| **PAY** | 8 | Can we legally and reliably pay them? Rails, FX control, sanctions |
| **EOR** | 8 | EOR infrastructure at sane wholesale cost — 37-65% of lifetime GP |
| **WHITE** | 7 | Whitespace. Is the pool already fished by Somewhere / Oceans / Wing? |
| **GAAP** | 7 | US-GAAP exposure — has this workforce kept American books? |
| **OURADV** | 6 | Do WE have a network and cost base there? |
| **STABLE** | 5 | Power, internet, security, political continuity |
| **TZ** | 5 | US-hours overlap. Deliberately low: every role is async by gate |

**Three of these weights are the whole argument:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **RETAIN is heaviest (20)** | Seat continuity is the largest lever in the business — **+$9,022 of gross profit per client** going from 9 to 30 EOR months, 18x what halving CAC delivers ([`scoring/LTGP.md`](scoring/LTGP.md) §4). And retention is not a cultural trait, it is **the worker's outside options** — so RETAIN is really a measure of local labour-market slack |
| **TZ is nearly weightless (5)** | **ASYNC is a hard gate in the skill model** ([`scoring/FIRST-PRINCIPLES.md`](scoring/FIRST-PRINCIPLES.md)). Every role we place works without live overlap. Weighting timezone highly would mean paying a premium for something we deliberately gated out — **and that premium is exactly what LatAm charges** |
| **GAAP means US-GAAP *exposure*** | Not which framework the country reports under — almost everyone is IFRS. The question is whether the workforce has actually kept American books. Prague was dropped on this ([`OFFER.md`](OFFER.md) §2.4) |

### The gates

| Gate | Fails if | Why it is a gate, not a score |
|---|---|---|
| **ENG** | < 3 | cannot brief a US client |
| **PAY** | < 2 | cannot pay them reliably or legally |
| **EOR** | < 2 | no EOR layer = lose 37-65% of lifetime GP |
| **STABLE** | < 2 | delivery risk on a guaranteed seat |

Applied **after** weighting, so a fatal flaw cannot be averaged away by strengths elsewhere.

---

## 2. The EF EPI caveat — read this before the ranking

**EF EPI measures a national *average*. We recruit the top 1%.** Those are different quantities,
and conflating them would produce a badly wrong answer:

| | EF EPI 2025 | What it hides |
|---|---|---|
| **India** | **484 — Low band** | 1.4 billion people and an enormous English-medium educated class. **The absolute number of excellent English speakers in India exceeds the entire population of most countries in this table** |
| **Sri Lanka** | **486 — Low band** | **Oceans built an entire company sourcing Sri Lanka and nothing else** [V] |
| **Egypt** | **459 — Low band** | Somewhere sells Egypt [V] |
| **Rwanda** | **417 — Very Low** | English is an *official language*. Official status is not proficiency |

So `ENG` in this model is **EPI adjusted for the depth of the top of the distribution**, which is
why India scores 4 on a 484 and Ghana scores 3 on a 540. The raw EPI is shown in every table so
you can see where the override happened. **Where EPI is genuinely decisive is at the bottom:** a
country at 440 has no usable tail for client-facing work at our volumes.

## 4. The top five, with the evidence

### 1. India — 80.9

528,000+ active CAs [V] · attrition 13.6% forecast 2026, but a 20-30% hike triggers a switch at early-to-mid level [V]

**The incumbent choice. Deepest pool, our own network, and untouched by both direct comps — but the leakiest, because the domestic market bids for the same people.**

### 2. South Africa — 74.5

EF EPI 602, **13th globally** [V] · unemployment **32.7%** Q1 2026, youth 15-34 **45.8%** [V] · ~**half of graduates** unemployed or underemployed in year one [V] · SAICA 48,000+ members, SAIPA 10,000+ [V]

**The retention answer. Structurally sticky because outside options barely exist.**

### 3. Nigeria — 74.5

EF EPI 569 [V] · ICAN is one of Africa's largest accountancy bodies

**Biggest English-speaking pool in Africa and the cheapest. FX controls, power, and US-client perception are the whole problem.**

### 4. Kenya — 72.0

EF EPI 593, 19th globally [V] · English is an official language of instruction

**The sleeper. High English, real professional body (ICPAK), payment rails work, and almost nobody in this category is there yet.**

### 5. Jamaica — 69.5

**Native English** · not ranked by EF EPI (English is the first language) · US Eastern timezone year-round

**Native English on US hours. A population of 2.8 million is the entire problem.**

## 6. Does the answer survive different weights?

The ranking is only useful if it is not an artefact of my weights.

| If you weighted... | 1st | 2nd | 3rd |
|---|---|---|---|
| As modelled | India | South Africa | Nigeria |
| **TZ heavily (20)** — if you did NOT believe async | India | Jamaica | South Africa |
| **COST heavily (25)** — pure arbitrage | India | Nigeria | South Africa |
| **RETAIN doubled (40)** | South Africa | Nigeria | India |
| **ENG heavily (30)** | India | South Africa | Nigeria |
| **OURADV to zero** — ignore our India edge | India | South Africa | Nigeria |
| **WHITE heavily (20)** — avoid contested pools | India | Nigeria | Kenya |

**The top of the table is stable under every reweighting except a heavy timezone weight** — which
is the one weight the async gate says you should not apply.

---

## 7. Three findings that matter more than the order

### 7.1 India and South Africa are not competing on the same axis

| | India | South Africa |
|---|---|---|
| **Pool of qualified accountants** | **528,000+ CAs** [V] | SAICA 48,000 + SAIPA 10,000 [V] — **~9x shallower** |
| **EF EPI 2025** | 484 — Low band | **602 — 13th globally**, Very High |
| **Why they stay** | They don't especially. **A 20-30% hike triggers a switch at early-to-mid level** [V] — exactly our band | **32.7% unemployment; ~half of graduates unemployed or underemployed in year one** [V]. There is no counter-bid |
| **Who else is fishing there** | **Neither Somewhere nor Oceans sources India** [V] | On Somewhere's published country list [V] — and every EOR vendor is now marketing it |
| **Our own position** | Network, language, cost base | Foreign recruiter, no network |
| **US-GAAP exposure** | 30 years of US accounting outsourcing | Thinner — historically UK/IFRS-facing, not US |

**India sells depth. South Africa sells retention.** And the model says retention is worth more —
+$9,022 per client from 9 to 30 EOR months, against a shallower pool that still contains 58,000
qualified accountants for a business that needs to place **~250 people to reach $10M**. *Depth we
do not need is not an advantage.*

The counter-argument is real and it is not about talent: **in India we have a network and a local
cost base; in South Africa we would be a foreign recruiter buying candidates at arm's length.**
That is a real cost, and it is an execution cost rather than a structural one.

### 7.2 The LatAm timezone premium is a premium for something we gated out

| Country | EF EPI 2025 | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Mexico | **440** | **Very Low** |
| Colombia | **480** | Low |
| Brazil | **482** | Low |
| Costa Rica | **516** | Moderate |
| Argentina | **575** | High |
| Honduras | **553** | High |

**Mexico at 440 is the weakest English of any country that is actively marketed as a nearshore
destination** — only Rwanda (417) scores lower anywhere in the screen, and nobody sells
Rwanda for this. Colombia at 480 scores **below Nepal (514) and Bangladesh (506)**.
**9 of the 12 Latin American countries screened are gated out on English alone.**

Latin America's real product is the timezone. **We gated timezone out when we made ASYNC a hard
requirement**, so we would be paying LatAm prices for a benefit the offer does not use. The two
exceptions are genuine: **Argentina (575, best in the Americas)** and **Honduras (553, second-best,
above Chile, Peru, Colombia and Brazil)** — and Honduras has almost no professional depth.

### 7.3 A USD salary is a retention mechanism, and it is strongest where payment is hardest

In a country with a depreciating currency, a **USD-denominated salary compounds in local terms** while
the worker's local peers are eroded. That is a golden handcuff nobody has to fund — the same logic
as provident fund and gratuity in the EOR line ([`OFFER.md`](OFFER.md)), but stronger and free.

**The problem is that it is exactly correlated with bad payment rails.** Zimbabwe, Nigeria, Argentina
and Egypt are where a USD wage is worth the most and where getting money in and employing people
legally is hardest. **That correlation is why the `PAY` and `EOR` gates do most of the work in this
screen** — and why Zimbabwe, at a pre-gate 69.1 with world-class English and retention, does not
appear in the ranking at all.

---

## 8. What this actually recommends

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stay in India for the launch** | Not because it wins the model by 6 points — that is inside the noise — but because `OURADV` is the only dimension we cannot buy, and at pre-launch, execution risk dominates optimisation |
| **Open South Africa as country two, for retention** | Same roles, same ledger spine. Test it on the *replacement* seats first, where a 30-month seat is worth $9,022 and a leaked hire costs the guarantee |
| **Watch Kenya** | 593 EPI, working rails, real accountancy body, and **the only high-scoring country in the study that is neither contested nor gated**. It is the cheapest place to run a 5-candidate test |
| **Ignore LatAm unless a client demands live overlap** | 9 of the 12 screened fail the English gate. The one thing LatAm sells, we do not buy |
| **Do not touch Nigeria or Zimbabwe yet** | Both would rank top-3 on talent alone. Both sit on or below the `PAY` gate. Revisit only once the EOR partner question is answered |

**The honest limit of this screen:** `RETAIN`, `GAAP`, `WHITE` and `OURADV` are `[E]` judgements. Only
`ENG` (EF EPI 2025), South Africa's unemployment figures, India's attrition series and the accountancy
body memberships are `[V]`. **The cheap way to convert this to fact is the supply test already in
[`README.md`](README.md): post one role, count qualified applicants in 72 hours — run it in three
countries at once for ~$900 instead of one for $300.**
